title: Slow Harriet
lead: Chief Marrow says the Slow Harriet burns more fuel than any two ships in the fleet and ought to be stripped for parts. Her caretaker, a seventy-nine-year-old named Bellamy Orr, says you're welcome to come aboard and discuss it, but please wipe your feet.
anyone: Chief Marrow says the Slow Harriet burns more fuel than any two ships in the fleet and ought to be stripped for parts. Her caretaker, a seventy-nine-year-old named Bellamy Orr, says anyone's welcome to come aboard and discuss it, as long as they wipe their feet.

gm.truth: The Slow Harriet is listed as an old bulk carrier with nine hundred passengers, and they're there, crammed into her upper holds. Sealed Hold C holds 240 cold-sleep pods: the Concord's continuity of government. Seventy-one senators, three high court judges, Deputy First Minister Ottilie Renn, staff, families and forty children, loaded in secret days before the end. That's where the fuel goes, because the pods are old and greedy. Bellamy Orr, senior usher of the Senate, is the only one awake who knows. He dusts the pods, and he reads them the news every morning so they won't be behind, including the casualty lists. The moment Renn wakes she's head of government, the captain's appointment is void, and so is Halm's council. And Halm isn't on the list: his colleagues left him behind on purpose, and he thinks he's the last. Stripping the ship, the sensible thing everyone's asking for, would kill all 240 and all the captain's rivals, and only Orr would know. The pods have about a month left without a lot more fuel than the fleet can spare.
beats: Marrow's case: the numbers. The fleet is worse off every day she flies. The nine hundred upstairs are furious at how crammed they are.
Bellamy Orr and his immaculate manners. He has the only clean carpet in the fleet, and he insists on announcing the captain properly, to a locked door.
Hold C. Row on row of sleeping faces, a chair and a stack of news sheets. He has just reached the part where he reads them the fleet's fuel figures.
He explains what it means, with a certain dry relish. Then he asks how the captain would like to be announced.
The choice: strip her, keep her, wake them all or wake one.
routes: Engineering and void_ops: cut the pods' draw, or get to Hold C from outside to see what can be done. Perhaps half the fuel, with risks for a fifth of the pods.
Lore and persuasion: Concord constitutional law, and a long talk with Orr about what the law would really require. He knows it better than anyone alive, and he has views.

Politics: tell Halm, or don't. Hacking the pods' locks lets the captain wake just one: a judge, perhaps, if the fleet needs a real one (see fleet_bunk_forty_one), or a senator who owes nobody anything.
Let it happen quietly: commerce and deception, moving the fuel elsewhere on paper. No one would ever know.
checks: composure:easy to keep a straight face through the announcing
lore:hard to work out what happens the moment Renn wakes
engineering:hard to cut the pods' draw without losing any
void_ops:moderate to reach Hold C from the hull
hacking:hard to open one pod without waking the rest
deception:moderate to lose the Slow Harriet's fuel on paper
fights: security_drone pair guarding Hold C, if the captain comes in any way except through the door with their feet wiped
outcomes: Stripped: fuel for three jumps and all the parts Marrow could want. Orr stands in the cold hold and reads them the news a last time, then asks politely what he should do with himself. Only the two of them will ever know. Let it be heavy.
Kept flying: the fleet pays the fuel, and the captain has 240 rivals asleep and a month to decide. Orr brings the captain the news sheets with small corrections.

Woken: a government returns, baffled and outraged, demanding a briefing. Some are useless. Renn is a decent, frightened woman who asks the captain for the truth, privately. The captain is now a subordinate, or a rebel, or both. Halm's face when he reads the list is something to see. Admiral Okonkwo-Reyes, who has been looking for the Concord's government at Project Harbor, will want to know how long it has been in the captain's hold.
One woken: Justice Ameline Thorne, a Thessan, awake and appalled, and the fleet has its first real judge. She'll want to know who else is in there, and she's going to find out.
gm.rewards: refined_fuel if she's stripped. An old_concord_medal from Orr, pressed into the captain's hand, if they showed respect. A long look at what legitimacy means.
